Gelvonai Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Vilnius County, Lithuania

Demolished. This record shows a tension worth noting: it is categorized as 'fenced and protected,' yet the source's demolished field marks it as 'yes.' One of Gelvonai's surviving gravestones dates back to 1659, though Jews are documented settling there from the 17th century more broadly; before WWI, the town was considered prosperous, with about 90 Jewish families making up 90 percent of the population by 1914. After the German invasion in 1941, Lithuanian nationalists looted Jewish homes, though a local priest publicly condemned the thieves and some property was returned; on September 5, 1941, all of Gelvonai's Jews were murdered in the Pivonija forest.
